messages:
Maya: Heads-up: we need a compact surge-mode runbook for Q3. Purpose: clear gates, simple canary signals, and fallback flows so CS/sales and on-call know exactly what will happen during promos or bursts.

Alex: +1. Are we covering scheduled promos and unplanned spikes in the same doc? We should call out different windows/thresholds.

Maya: Yes — single playbook with 'scheduled' and 'ad-hoc' variants. Keep steps actionable.

Sam: Outline proposal:
- Canary signals (p95, p99, error %, token/sec, and a light quality check)
- Kernel fallback order + perf delta table
- Quantization rollback triggers (when to revert int4->int8 or switch model family)
- KV cache eviction policy under GPU memory pressure
- Routing priorities (reserved / best-effort / emergency cached responses)
- Per-customer burst buckets & throttle overrides

Jordan: Also: include an 'operator quick checklist' with 6 steps (triage, canary evaluation, decide fallback, apply routing, monitor 15m, escalate).

Olivia: For quality signal, propose a micro-eval (30 queries) run against a small canonical eval-set and track pass-rate + perplexity delta. Don’t auto-roll back on small noisy diffs.

Ben: Customer anecdote: last month a large account hit p99 > 2s due to KV thrash. Short-term mitigation was aggressive prefix eviction which dropped memory pressure but increased tokens generated. Need explicit eviction thresholds and safe defaults.

Maya: Draft canary snippet (copy/paste friendly):
```
canary:
  type: scheduled|ad-hoc
  window: 10m # scheduled, 5m for ad-hoc
  p95_ms: 250
  p99_ms: 700
  error_pct: 0.5
  quality_fail_pct: <=0.8
  min_tokens_per_sec: 12k
  fallback_route: family-small-v2
  kv_eviction_pct_of_gpu_mem: 12
```

Alex: Change: window should be param per cluster size. Suggest commenting: "adjust window to 2x expected promo ramp time". And kv_eviction must be percent of GPU mem (not MB).

Sam: For kernel fallbacks include expected perf deltas and when to prefer them over routing. Example entry: "aten-fast -> generic-kernel: +20-35% latency at seq>8k; memory down slightly". We'll build a short table.

Olivia: Runbook rule proposals: 
- If quality regresses but latency OK -> rollback quantization or bump to larger model family.
- If latency regresses but quality OK -> apply kernel fallback or route reserved traffic to dedicated pool.
- If both poor -> emergency degrade: return cached responses or rate-limit non-SLA traffic.

Jordan: Routing policy draft (simple):
1) SLA/reserved -> reserved pools (no auto-degrade)
2) Gold/paid -> attempt reserved, fallback to compatible family if capacity constrained
3) Free/best-effort -> route to smallest compatible family or cache
4) Emergency -> serve cached responses / embeddings-only fallback

Ben: Customer KB blurb (short):
"During very large spikes we may temporarily route requests to smaller model families or return cached responses to maintain overall availability. Enterprise customers can opt into reserved capacity or purchase burst packs for guaranteed performance during promotions."

Maya: Ops automation notes: tie canary to both latency and quality signals. Alerts should require paired breaches (e.g., p95 breach + quality fail) before auto-rolling back heavy changes.

ops-bot: FYI: scheduled canary template added to infra repo: infra/surge/canaries/standard-window.yaml

deploy-bot: Reminder: document must include rollback commands for kernels/quant toggles and console UI config snippets.

Maya: Action items and owners:
- Sam: kernel perf appendix + microbench harness + perf numbers (due Tue)
- Olivia: define canonical eval-set + small-eval pass thresholds (due Tue)
- Ben: customer KB draft + 2 example scenarios (due Wed)
- Jordan: routing config snippets + console labels + default throttle presets (due Thu)
- Maya: assemble final playbook + publish to sprint doc (due Fri)

Alex: Add postmortem checklist item: capture model choice & capacity decision rationale for roadmap follow-up. Also save a snapshot of canary config used.

Maya: Good call. We'll include a 'post-event capture' short form in the playbook.

Olivia: :thumbsup:

Ben: I'll draft the KB and include an example where cached responses prevented downtime.

Sam: I'll start the perf table; will include kernel name, expected latency delta, memory delta, and recommended use-case.

Maya: Thanks everyone. I will tag reviewers when drafts are in.

Alex: one last note: keep the playbook short — operators need 60s to decide.

Maya: Agreed. We’ll make the front page a one-minute decision card and appendices for details.
